title: Polycarbonate / resin food-contact scenario
product: Selected polycarbonate or epoxy-resin food-contact materials
exposure: Potential migration into food followed by ingestion
molecular_target: ERα / ERβ and related estrogen-signaling pathways
mechanism: BPA can interact with estrogen-signaling pathways in experimental systems. Biological consequences depend on dose, timing, tissue and exposure context.
evidence_label: Mechanistically established; health-effect claims are endpoint-specific
caveat: This pathway is a studied mechanism, not proof that every plastic product contains BPA or that ordinary use produces a specific adverse effect.

title: Flexible vinyl / PVC scenario
product: Selected flexible PVC and vinyl materials
exposure: Ingestion of contaminated food or dust; inhalation and dermal contact can also contribute
mechanism: DEHP metabolites are studied for effects on PPAR signaling, lipid metabolism and steroid hormone synthesis, with developmental timing especially important in reproductive toxicology.
caveat: Phthalates are not interchangeable. Exposure is often assessed through metabolites, and DEHP findings should not be generalized to every phthalate.

title: Drinking-water PFAS scenario
mechanism: PFOA has been studied for effects on lipid-regulatory signaling and thyroid-related endpoints. Mechanisms and human relevance vary by endpoint and dose.
source_label: U.S. EPA — PFAS Human Health Risks
caveat: PFOA findings cannot be generalized to the thousands of other PFAS, and exposure concentration is essential to risk interpretation.

title: Water-resistant textile scenario
product: A textile confirmed to use a PFAS treatment
exposure: Dermal contact, transferred dust, or indirect environmental exposure
molecular_target: Thyroid-hormone homeostasis and nuclear-receptor signaling under study
mechanism: Selected PFAS have been investigated for thyroid and metabolic effects, but the relevant mechanism depends on the actual compound and internal dose.
source_label: U.S. EPA — PFAS Human Health Risks
caveat: A 'water-resistant' label is not evidence that a particular PFAS is present. Use this pathway only when product chemistry or analytical testing identifies the chemical.

title: Legacy DDT / DDE dietary scenario
product: Food or environmental media containing legacy DDT metabolites
mechanism: p,p′-DDE is a well-known antiandrogenic compound in experimental systems and is studied for reproductive and developmental endocrine effects.
evidence_label: Strong mechanistic basis; epidemiology varies by endpoint
caveat: A receptor mechanism does not automatically establish the magnitude of effect at a real-world exposure level.

title: Indoor dust / legacy foam scenario
product: Older foam, furnishings or indoor dust containing PBDEs
exposure: Dust ingestion, inhalation and dermal contact
molecular_target: Thyroid-hormone transport, metabolism and receptor-related signaling
mechanism: PBDEs and their metabolites have been studied for interference with thyroid-hormone homeostasis through several mechanisms, including transport and metabolism.
evidence_label: Substantial experimental evidence; human outcomes are endpoint-specific
caveat: Flame retardants are chemically diverse. Evidence for PBDEs should not be transferred to every flame-retardant chemical.

title: Older-building PCB scenario
product: Older caulk, electrical materials or indoor environments with confirmed PCB contamination
exposure: Inhalation, dust ingestion or dietary exposure
mechanism: Non-dioxin-like PCBs such as PCB-153 are studied for effects on thyroid-hormone homeostasis and neuroendocrine development rather than through a single receptor mechanism.
source_label: U.S. EPA — Health Effects of PCBs
caveat: PCB congeners differ substantially. PCB-153 is not a proxy for every PCB or for all dioxin-like mechanisms.

title: Personal-care phthalate scenario
product: A personal-care formulation containing a relevant phthalate
exposure: Dermal contact; incidental ingestion or inhalation may contribute
mechanism: DBP is studied for reproductive and developmental effects involving disrupted androgen-dependent development and steroidogenesis.
caveat: A product category alone does not identify DBP exposure; the formulation or analytical measurement must establish the ingredient.
